season_futures#bowl_eligibility_rule.evidence: The structure is fixed: cfb.bowl_selection_state measurement now caps countable FCS wins with min(1, ...), raw_data carries opponent division, FCS aid/waiver, APR and reclassification status, and season_futures stage s7 plus required_data[4] match. But the central corrected fact is wrong. cfb.bowl_selection_state rationale/measurement and stage s7 use an FCS-opponent threshold of '80% of the maximum grants-in-aid' and s7 says 'the old 90% figure is obsolete'. The NCAA Sep 2022 D-I Council report (checked directly) says the Council adopted Proposal 2022-22 to raise that requirement 'from 80 percent ... to 90 percent of the permissible maximum number of grants-in-aid per year during a rolling two-year period' (Aug 2022 FOC report: effective 2023-24). The 80% figure was the 2020 COVID waiver described in the FOC 2022-03-24 report that the resolver cited. So the model uses an expired threshold and calls the current one obsolete, which misclassifies bubble teams. Proposal 2026-30 (conference picks any 930+ APR 5-7 team instead of APR order) matches the FBSOC May 2026 reports. I could not confirm the June Cabinet adoption or 2026-31 because ncaa.org is unreachable from this session. Fix: change to 90% in the input and in s7, and cite Proposal 2022-22.

season_futures#committee_model_duplicati.evidence: The duplication is resolved. Catalog cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model measurement now merges both feature lists: head-to-head and common opponents, starting-QB injury flag, pre/post-championship weights, pairwise-ordering calibration and per-release rank output. cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features is redefined as an alias ('Not computed separately: read the rank distribution output of cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model') and carries audit_flag DUPLICATE. The season_futures and polls records give identical definitions for the canonical id; the polls record audits the alias as DUPLICATE_OF:cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model, and every stage, coverage, interaction and required_data reference uses the canonical id. Leftovers, none of which gives a diverging definition: (1) catalog unregistered polls_and_cfp_rankings still attaches the alias as a primary input (inputs[13]), and interactions[5] still uses it, because integrate never removes inputs; (2) the canonical raw_data and free_sources do not list an injury-status source even though the merged measurement uses a QB injury flag.

touchdown_scorer#player_series_missing.evidence: I checked the live Kalshi /trade-api/v2/series list (Sports, 4156 series) on 2026-11-08. College football has only KXNCAAFTEAMTD, TOTALTD, TEAMRSHTD, TEAMRECTD, DSTTD and FIRSTTDTEAM, and no named-player TD series; the NFL has KXNFLANYTD and KXNFLFIRSTTD. series_assignment.json files all six CFB series under game_stat_props (ledger_archetype touchdown_scorer, origin reviewed). In the catalog, game_stat_props now attaches cfb.td_per_scoring_trip, td_count_dispersion, dst_td_propensity, first_td_race_rate and goal_to_go_run_pass_mix as primary. All five are used in stage s7 ('Touchdown counts and the first-touchdown race'), and the contract_review covers the TD settlement. The touchdown_scorer contract_review reads NO_LIVE_SERIES, with td_rates, player_usage and depth_chart audited WEAK. Leftover: the catalog touchdown_scorer inputs still list td_rates and player_usage as primary (integrate cannot rewrite roles). This is disclosed in its unresolved entry and does not affect the live series mapping.
